subject: nimble stuck on 'running calculate on model' on multi-site robust design CMR model

messages.author: bfa4a88c8a5bc54e
messages.subject: nimble stuck on 'running calculate on model' on multi-site robust design CMR model
parts:
Hello all,

I've just gotten started on nimble after using JAGS for the past year. I've learned a lot already and am keen to put some of its additional functionality to use. I'm trying to fit a multi-site robust design multistate CMR model, with multiple secondary occasions for each primary occasion, two disease states, and capture histories at three sites. My observation array y has four dimensions, specifically y[individual, primary occasion, secondary survey, site]. The nimble user manual section 5.1.1 says 4-dimensional arrays are handled fine, although I'm not sure if the resulting 6-dimensional matrices for state transitions and observations are handled fine as well. 

When trying to create a nimble model through nimbleModel(), nimble appears to freeze after:

defining model...
building model...
setting data and initial values...
running calculate on model (any error reports that follow may simply reflect missing values in model variables) ...

The same thing happens when using the nimbleMCMC() function. When I remove the multiple sites, there's no problem and nimble runs just fine. It's just when including the multiple sites that nimble freezes. I'll also add that JAGS is unable to run this model (it freezes), and that so far OpenBUGS is the only program that plays nice.

I've got an R script with capture history simulation, nimble model code, constants, etc. that I'd prefer to share off-list. If anyone would like to help diagnose the problem, I'd be very grateful. 

Kind regards,
Matt Hollanders

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: nimble stuck on 'running calculate on model' on multi-site robust design CMR model
parts:
Hi Matt,

Thanks for posting.  As a quick reply, please try using "calculate = FALSE" in the call to nimbleModel.  

By default (calculate = TRUE), nimbleModel iterates through every node of the model, in order, trying to calculate, which means calculating values for deterministic nodes and log probabilities for stochastic nodes.  For large models, this can take a long time because it is uncompiled and also doing some laborious keeping track of model structure.  It can be helpful for debugging or catching issues, but it isn't strictly necessary. 

-Perry
